knowledge_point.title: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=2 x + 3 y + 3 z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨3 u^{2},\,u - v^{2},\,v^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ Assume $v\geq0.$ What is the missing expression? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2 v \sqrt{72 u^{2} + 1}.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2 v \sqrt{72 u^{2} + 1}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(2 x + 3 y + 3 z)\,{|}_{x=3 u^{2}\,y=u - v^{2}\,z=v^{2}} \\  & =2\cdot (3 u^{2})+3\cdot ((u-v^{2})+v^{2}) \\  & =6 u^{2} + 3 u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2 v \sqrt{72 u^{2} + 1} \left(6 u^{2} + 3 u\right)\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=3 x - y^{2} z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨3 u v,\,- u,\,2 u - v^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(3 u v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(- u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2 u - v^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨3 v,\,-1,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(3 u v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(- u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2 u - v^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨3 u,\,0,\,- 2 v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 3 v & -1 & 2 \\ 3 u & 0 & - 2 v\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & - 2 v\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}3 v & 2 \\ 3 u & - 2 v\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}3 v & -1 \\ 3 u & 0\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨2 v,\,6 u + 6 v^{2},\,3 u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨2 v,\,6 u + 6 v^{2},\,3 u⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(2 v)^{2}+(6 u + 6 v^{2})^{2}+(3 u)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{45 u^{2} + 72 u v^{2} + 36 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(3 x - y^{2} z)\,{|}_{x=3 u v\,y=- u\,z=2 u - v^{2}} \\  & =9 u v-1\cdot (- u)^{2}\cdot (2 u - v^{2}) \\  & =- 2 u^{3} + u^{2} v^{2} + 9 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\left(- 2 u^{3} + u^{2} v^{2} + 9 u v\right) \sqrt{45 u^{2} + 72 u v^{2} + 36 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(3 u^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨9 u^{2},\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(3 u^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2 v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 9 u^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 v\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 v\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}9 u^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 2 v\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}9 u^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,- 18 u^{2} v,\,9 u^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,- 18 u^{2} v,\,9 u^{2}⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(- 18 u^{2} v)^{2}+(9 u^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{324 u^{4} v^{2}+81 u^{4}} \\  & =9 u^{2} \sqrt{4 v^{2} + 1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(- 2 x - 3 z^{2})\,{|}_{x=3 u^{3}\,y=v\,z=v^{2}} \\  & =-2\cdot (3 u^{3})-3\cdot (v^{2}\cdot v^{2}) \\  & =- 6 u^{3} - 3 v^{4}\end{aligned}

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,9 u^{2} \sqrt{4 v^{2} + 1} \left(- 6 u^{3} - 3 v^{4}\right)\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨2 v,\,6 v^{2},\,3 u⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(2 v)^{2}+(6 v^{2})^{2}+(3 u)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9 u^{2} + 36 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}}.\end{aligned}

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(2 x - 3 y^{2} z)\,{|}_{x=3 u v\,y=- u\,z=- v^{2}} \\  & =2\cdot (3 u v)-3\cdot (-u)^{2}\cdot (-v^{2}) \\  & =3 u^{2} v^{2} + 6 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\left(3 u^{2} v^{2} + 6 u v\right) \sqrt{9 u^{2} + 36 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \left(3 u^{2} v^{2} + 6 u v\right) \left(9 u^{2} + 36 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}\right)

question.:question/problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=2 x^{2} z^{2} + 3 y$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨- 3 u,\,- u,\,- v⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(- 3 u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(- u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(- v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(- 3 u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(- u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(- v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ -3 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}-3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-3,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨1,\,-3,\,0⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(2 x^{2} z^{2} + 3 y)\,{|}_{x=- 3 u\,y=- u\,z=- v} \\  & =2\cdot (- 3 u)^{2}\cdot (-v)^{2}+3\cdot (-u) \\  & =18 u^{2} v^{2} - 3 u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\sqrt{10} \left(18 u^{2} v^{2} - 3 u\right)\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$
